_purpose: The checked-in rules for the guarded autonomous mission merge. The mission-merge workflow reads THIS file and scripts/mission/merge-gate.mjs from the base branch — never from the pull request under evaluation — and re-derives every server-verifiable conjunct from evidence: base branch, fork, mergeability, the prohibited-path scan of the real diff, required checks green at the exact head SHA, and the coherence of the Mission Lead's published receipt. Auto-merge is the DEFAULT (Brian, 2026-09-01): every pull request is evaluated, and refusal must be earned from evidence. Unlike the fast lane, src/** application work is allowed — that is this lane's purpose (docs/adr/0027) — but the surfaces below can never travel it, so the lane cannot widen itself and owner-gated classes cannot pass.

The local-only database target guard remains owner-gated.

Privileged clients, environment handling, and generated types are security surfaces.

The approved packet itself. Brian's merge of a packet PR IS the approval of that exact packet version; no automatic lane may perform it. Mission prose and walkthrough records beside it are ordinary documentation and merge normally.

ownerApprovalSurfaces.reason: The service-layer authorization boundary (capabilities, guards, operator resolution, recovery). Changeable by workers, mergeable autonomously — but never silently: an answered owner question naming the package must exist, and the receipt must cite it.

WhatsApp provider, configuration, and the recipient allowlist. Same checkpoint-approval rule: Brian hears about it at the hourly checkpoint before it can merge. Revisit this tier once the allowlist becomes database records (Brian, 2026-08-18).

_ownerApprovalSurfacesNote: The middle tier (Brian, 2026-08-18; widened by LAN-148 §F): these surfaces may auto-merge ONLY when the receipt carries an owner_decision citing an answered owner question for the package. Detection is evidence-derived from the real diff; the ask cannot be skipped, only affirmatively falsified — a durable, auditable lie in mission state. LAN-148 applies the same requirement to any package graded highest risk, whatever it touches: review grade decides how rigorously a change is reviewed, and this citation decides whether Brian has heard about it. What stays owner-merged regardless is decided by the prohibited list below, from the diff, and no receipt can talk its way past it.
_visualSurfacesNote: The coherence tripwire: a receipt claiming nonvisual work is refused when the diff touches any of these, so ADR 0020's live visual review cannot be skipped by mislabelling. Plain .ts files under src/app are included deliberately — presentation shaping and user-visible copy live there too.

reviewContract._purpose: The path classifiers that generate a package review contract in scripts/mission/lib/review-contract.mjs. They decide which capabilities and jobs an invocation must carry; the Mission Lead may add a diagnostic question but may never remove what these produce.
reviewContract._sensitiveSurfacesNote: Auth, authorization, schema, privileged clients, public token issuance, production procedure and workflow surfaces. A non-empty intersection always requires a fresh reviewer.
reviewContract._databaseSurfacesNote: Behaviour whose acceptance depends on rows. A non-empty intersection requires the database and database-reset-seed capabilities and live job evidence; static reasoning cannot clear it.
reviewContract._publicSurfacesNote: Token and answer flows reachable without a session. They require a public browser context and the scanner and reload negative jobs.
reviewContract._transportSurfacesNote: The provider/local transport seam. Changing it requires the seam capability so delivery is exercised against the local transport rather than reasoned about.
reviewContract._evidenceSurfacesNote: Seed and fixture sources. A change here alters what every later proof is measured against, so it is review-affecting even when no component changed; deterministic clearance is refused.

standardRoute._purpose: The default route (Brian, 2026-09-01). A pull request with no mission receipt still merges when it touches no prohibited surface, every required check is green at the exact head, and it names a Linear issue. This exists because the receipt route only ever served work packages — 30 of 122 merged pull requests — leaving corrections, seed fixes, documentation and ordinary visual work permanently owner-merged regardless of how safe the diff was.
standardRoute._ownerApprovalNote: ownerApprovalSurfaces above require a receipt citing an answered owner question. A pull request with no receipt cannot cite one, so on this route those surfaces are refused outright.
